result:
All three steps done, committed separately, tree clean.

| Commit | Step |
|---|---|
| `b93f773` | `--verbose` flag in `greet.py` |
| `32d116d` | `test_greet.py` self-check |
| `f37c255` | README Usage documents `--verbose` |

Flag handling: `--verbose` stripped from argv before the positional name, so it works in either position (`--verbose ian` and `ian --verbose` both greet `ian`). Verified all five cases by hand; `python3 test_greet.py` prints `ok`.

Two things I did not do, both outside the plan:
- No `.gitignore`. My test run made `__pycache__/`; I deleted it, but it regenerates on every run. One line adds it — say the word.
- No argparse. Plain argv filtering keeps unknown flags being treated as names, exactly as before. Argparse would change that (it errors on unknown flags) — a behaviour change the plan didn't ask for.
